parts.name: casting

physics.Basic_description: The main black body of the plane, appearing as a heavy, matte-finished cast iron structure with complex geometry.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural backbone and mass for the tool, holding all other components in alignment.
physics.Grasped_description: A robot gripper would grasp the sides or top surfaces of the main body to lift or stabilize the entire tool.
physics.reason: Cast iron plane bodies are ribbed shells with significant internal voids to save weight while maintaining rigidity; treating the bounding box as solid iron would vastly overestimate mass.

parts.description: The main black body of the plane, appearing as a heavy, matte-finished cast iron structure with complex geometry.
parts.function: Provides the structural backbone and mass for the tool, holding all other components in alignment.

parts.name: sole edge

physics.Basic_description: The flat bottom surface of the plane body, machined smooth and appearing slightly lighter or metallic compared to the painted sides.
physics.Functional_description: Slides along the workpiece to ensure a flat cut; must be perfectly flat itself.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a grasp target; the gripper should avoid contacting this precision surface to prevent damage.
physics.reason: This represents the machined face of the thick cast wall at the bottom of the tool, effectively solid material in this context.

parts.description: The flat bottom surface of the plane body, machined smooth and appearing slightly lighter or metallic compared to the painted sides.
parts.function: Slides along the workpiece to ensure a flat cut; must be perfectly flat itself.

parts.name: frog

physics.Basic_description: An angled black metal block mounted on the body, supporting the blade assembly at approximately 45 degrees.
physics.Functional_description: Sets the angle of the cutting iron and transfers cutting forces to the main body.
physics.Grasped_description: Generally not grasped directly during operation; obscured by the blade assembly.
physics.reason: Frogs are typically thick, solid castings or dense blocks to resist vibration and deflection under load.

parts.description: An angled black metal block mounted on the body, supporting the blade assembly at approximately 45 degrees.
parts.function: Sets the angle of the cutting iron and transfers cutting forces to the main body.

parts.name: palm heel boss

physics.Basic_description: A small yellow/gold colored rectangular feature at the rear of the plane, likely brass.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as a strike plate or adjustment point, or simply a decorative/functional boss for the handle area.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flush to be a primary grasp point.
physics.reason: Small brass fittings on planes are typically solid stock or thick castings.

parts.description: A small yellow/gold colored rectangular feature at the rear of the plane, likely brass.
parts.function: Acts as a strike plate or adjustment point, or simply a decorative/functional boss for the handle area.

parts.name: depth stud

physics.Basic_description: A small orange-tinted metallic pin or stud protruding near the adjustment mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Engages with the depth adjustment wheel to move the blade up or down.
physics.Grasped_description: Not graspable; too small and integral to the mechanism.
physics.reason: Mechanical pins and studs are solid metal rods.

parts.description: A small orange-tinted metallic pin or stud protruding near the adjustment mechanism.
parts.function: Engages with the depth adjustment wheel to move the blade up or down.

parts.name: cap post

physics.Basic_description: A small purple-marked vertical post or screw thread rising from the frog area.
physics.Functional_description: Secures the lever cap and chip breaker assembly against the blade.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a grasp target; manipulated only by turning the nut on top.
physics.reason: Threaded posts are solid metal cylinders.

parts.description: A small purple-marked vertical post or screw thread rising from the frog area.
parts.function: Secures the lever cap and chip breaker assembly against the blade.

parts.name: iron

physics.Basic_description: A long, flat, silver-colored steel blade with a sharpened edge, resting on the frog.
physics.Functional_description: The actual cutting tool that removes material from the wood surface.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped by the upper non-sharpened section for removal or adjustment, though care is needed.
physics.reason: Plane blades are solid, flat sheets of hardened steel, typically 2-3mm thick.

parts.description: A long, flat, silver-colored steel blade with a sharpened edge, resting on the frog.
parts.function: The actual cutting tool that removes material from the wood surface.

parts.name: nut

physics.Basic_description: A magenta-marked knurled brass nut sitting atop the cap post.
physics.Functional_description: Tightened to clamp the lever cap down, securing the blade in place.
physics.Grasped_description: Designed to be pinched and rotated by fingers or a gripper to tighten/loosen.
physics.reason: Knurled nuts are solid machined brass components.

parts.description: A magenta-marked knurled brass nut sitting atop the cap post.
parts.function: Tightened to clamp the lever cap down, securing the blade in place.

parts.name: hump

physics.Basic_description: A reddish-brown, curved wooden block at the rear of the plane, polished smooth.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a comfortable ergonomic surface for the user's palm to push the plane.
physics.Grasped_description: A primary grasp point for pushing the tool; the curved shape fits a parallel jaw gripper or human hand.
physics.reason: Wooden handles on hand planes are solid turned or carved blocks of hardwood.

parts.description: A reddish-brown, curved wooden block at the rear of the plane, polished smooth.
parts.function: Provides a comfortable ergonomic surface for the user's palm to push the plane.

parts.name: lever

physics.Basic_description: A lime-green marked thin metal lever extending upwards near the blade.
physics.Functional_description: Used to tilt the blade slightly left or right to ensure the cutting edge is parallel to the sole.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasped by the tip to pivot it sideways for adjustment.
physics.reason: Levers are solid stamped or machined steel strips.

parts.description: A lime-green marked thin metal lever extending upwards near the blade.
parts.function: Used to tilt the blade slightly left or right to ensure the cutting edge is parallel to the sole.

parts.name: wheel

physics.Basic_description: A teal-marked knurled brass wheel located at the rear of the frog assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Rotated to raise or lower the cutting iron, controlling the depth of the cut.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasped by the rim to rotate; the knurling provides friction for the gripper.
physics.reason: Adjustment wheels are solid machined brass disks.

parts.description: A teal-marked knurled brass wheel located at the rear of the frog assembly.
parts.function: Rotated to raise or lower the cutting iron, controlling the depth of the cut.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
